posts.title: The bob, recut: why the sharp line is back
posts.excerpt: One-length, blunt and a little severe: the bob is the cut we do most this autumn. Mika on how to ask for it, and how to keep the line sharp.
posts.content:
Every few years the bob comes back, and every time it is a little sharper. This autumn, half the cuts in Mika’s chair have been some version of it: one length, a hard line at the jaw, and nothing feathered.

Scissors or razor?

A scissor-cut bob has a crisp, heavy edge and suits thick, straight hair. A razor softens the ends and helps fine hair move. We decide together at the consultation, by looking at your hair dry.

How to ask for it

  • Say where you want the line: lip, jaw or just below
  • Bring one photo you like, and one you do not
  • Tell us how you dry your hair on a normal morning

To keep the line sharp, book a short cut refresh every six weeks. It takes half an hour, and the bob never gets a grown-out stage.

posts.title: Neon gloss: how we keep magenta loud for six weeks
posts.excerpt: Vivid colour fades. Noa explains how we lay it down so it lasts, and the three habits at home that make the most difference.
posts.content:
Magenta is the loudest colour we mix, and the first to fade. Most of what makes it last happens in the chair; the rest is up to you.

In the chair

We lighten only as far as we need, with bond care in the bowl. Then the colour goes on thick and stays on longer than the box says. Noa weighs every formula and writes it on your card, so the next visit matches.

At home

  • Wash in cool water, two or three times a week at most
  • Use a sulphate-free shampoo, and skip clarifying ones
  • Add a few drops of the colour to your conditioner once a week

Do those three things and magenta stays bright for around six weeks. Swimming pools and strong sun will still take some of it, so a hat helps.

posts.title: Undercut geometry: drawing with clippers
posts.excerpt: A hidden undercut is a small canvas. Ren on grids, lines and how to grow one out without an awkward stage.
posts.content:
Lift a bob at the back and there is room for a picture. Ren has drawn grids, waves, single lines and once, by request, a tiny cat.

How it works

We take the nape short with clippers, then draw the design with a trimmer and a steady hand. It takes about twenty minutes. A design stays crisp for two to three weeks, and a quick tidy brings it back.

Growing it out

Let the design go soft for a month, then we blend it into the rest of the cut. Because the hair above covers it, nobody needs to know it was ever there.

posts.title: Curls, cut dry: what to expect
posts.excerpt: We cut curls dry, one by one, so they look right the way you actually wear them. Here is what happens in a dry-cut appointment.
posts.content:
Wet curls stretch, and a cut that looks perfect on wet hair can spring up far shorter when it dries. So we cut curls dry, in the shape you wear them.

Before you come

  • Arrive with your hair clean, dry and styled as usual
  • No tight buns or hats on the way, if you can
  • Bring the products you use, so we can see them

In the chair

We look at each curl, cut where it falls, and only then wash and style. The appointment takes about ninety minutes and ends with a lesson in drying, so it looks the same tomorrow.

posts.title: Five tools on every station at Kami
posts.excerpt: Combs, clips and not much else. A look at what sits on each stylist’s station, and which tools are worth having at home.
posts.content:
Every station at Kami holds the same short list. Nothing is there for show.

  • A wide-tooth comb, for detangling wet hair without breaking it
  • A tail comb, for sections and partings as straight as a ruler
  • Flat section clips; the magenta ones belong to Noa
  • One pair of scissors for cutting and one for texture
  • A water spray, used less than you would think

Worth having at home

A wide-tooth comb and two clips. That is genuinely it. Keep your hairdryer on medium heat and you will need fewer of the products on the shelf.

posts.title: Six chairs on the third floor
posts.excerpt: We doubled the room this summer: three new chairs, a second basin and a colour bar. The magenta wall stayed.
posts.content:
When Kami opened in 2019 there were three chairs and one basin, and the wait list grew faster than the hair. This summer we took over the rest of the third floor.

What is new

  • Three more cutting chairs, each with its own round mirror
  • A second basin, behind a curtain
  • A colour bar where every formula is weighed

What stayed the same: one stylist per client, a free consultation every time, and the magenta wall. Come and see it.
